data.name: Inesh
data.gender_notes: Inesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Inesh refers to the lord of mountains and the god of rain. He is also known as Indra, the god of thunder and rain. The name Inesh carries the meaning “Lord of the Mountain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Inesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mountain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, power, and divine protection.
data.etymology: Inesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Mountain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Inesh total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: In Hinduism, Inesh, also known as Indra, is considered a significant deity, revered for his role in providing rain and thus sustaining agriculture. He is believed to be the lord of mountains and the god of thunder, lightning, and the clouds. In many Hindu rituals and festivals, Indra is invoked to ensure a bountiful harvest. Additionally, in various regional folktales and literature, Indra is portrayed as a powerful warrior, capable of wielding thunderbolts and the rain clouds as his weapons.
data.spiritual_significance: Symbolizing the power of nature, Indra, or Inesh, embodies the profound importance of rain, agriculture, and the cyclical flow of life and energy. He serves as a reminder of our interconnectedness to nature's blessings. Indra's spiritual significance also underscores the virtues of perseverance, courage, and strength. The courage and power that Indra is known to possess in Hindu mythology encourages individuals to face life's challenges with determination and resilience. Furthermore, His association with rain and agriculture highlights the spiritual value of nourishing oneself and being mindful of the sustenance that nature provides.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Inesh: God's Grace and Compassion. It is believed that the name Inesh carries the blessings and protection of the divine, evoking feelings of love, kindness, and compassion.

historical_references.reference: Inesh was a noted Hindu scholar and philosopher during the Gupta Empire in the 5th century CE. His most famous work, the 'Yogavasishtha', is an important text in the Advaita Vedanta tradition.

Another reference suggests that Inesh was a king of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century CE. Details about his life and contributions are limited, but he is mentioned in various historical texts as a significant ruler.
